title: Water softener: get the control valve, motor and resin tank
summary: A home water softener gives you a control valve head with a small gear motor and timer board, a tall fibreglass resin tank, a 100–250 litre brine tank and often 20–100 kg of salt. Allow about 45 minutes. The main dangers are the water pressure still held in the tank and valve, and the weight of the salt and the wet resin.

steps.text: Look the unit over before touching it. You should find a tall resin tank with a control valve on top, a squat brine tank with a lid beside it, and pipes in and out. Find the bypass valve (a lever or two knobs at the back of the head) and a small plug-in transformer on a nearby socket. Photograph the pipes and tubing so you can see how it went together.
Unplug the transformer from the wall first, then from the head. Put the unit in bypass, or shut the inlet and outlet valves, so no more water can enter it.
steps.warn: The transformer has mains on its wall side. Pull it from the socket before you handle the head's wiring.

steps.text: Release the pressure. Open a cold tap downstream of the softener until the flow stops, then loosen the drain line or a pipe fitting at the head a little at a time, with a bucket under it. If the water supply is already dead the tank is probably at zero pressure, but check the same way.
steps.warn: The tank and valve can hold full supply pressure, often 3–6 bar. A fitting that lets go can hit hard and flood the room.

steps.text: Lift the lid off the brine tank. Scoop the salt out into buckets, sacks or bins and keep it dry and covered. Take the spare bags stacked beside it. Break up any hard crust with a stick.
steps.warn: A full brine tank can hold 100 kg or more of salt and water. Never lift or tip a full tank; empty it by the scoopful first.

steps.text: Pull the brine line (the thin tube from the brine well to the head) and the overflow hose off their fittings. Lift out the brine well and float valve (a tall tube with a float) and keep them with the tank. Pour the brine out slowly, well away from plants, wells and your water supply, then rinse the tank.

Take the cover off the control head (clips or 2–4 screws). Photograph the wiring, then unplug the motor lead, the board cable, the turbine meter lead (a thin cable from the outlet side) and any switch leads. Lift out the board and the gear motor. Keep the motor with its gear or cam if they come off together.

Undo the inlet and outlet pipes and the drain line at the bypass valve or head: unions, hose clamps or push-fit clips. Expect a cupful of water. Plastic fittings break easily; most undo by hand or with a gentle pull on the clip.

Unscrew the head from the tank. Most spin off anticlockwise by hand or with a strap wrench; some are held by a clamp ring. Lift it straight up so the distributor tube in the middle of the tank isn't bent or pulled out. Push a rag into the tank opening afterwards to keep out dirt and insects.
steps.warn: The tank thread is plastic. A pipe wrench cracks it. If the head is stuck, warm it with hot water and tap it round with a wooden block.

steps.text: Decide what to do with the resin tank. Full of resin and water it weighs about 30–70 kg and stands 1.2–1.5 m tall. To move it, tip it over a drain with a helper and let the water run out, plug the opening with a rag or bung, and carry it upright or on its side. Or scoop the resin into buckets of clean water and move the empty tank on its own.
steps.warn: Resin beads spilled on a hard floor act like ball bearings. Work on a tarp and sweep spills up at once.

steps.text: Keep the resin wet in sealed buckets, out of frost and sun. Good resin is tan, amber or brown beads. If it is black, slimy, crumbled or smells bad, leave it.

Test what you're keeping. Read the plug-in transformer's label for volts and whether the output is AC or DC, plug it in on its own and check the output with the meter set to match. Run the gear motor from the transformer or a battery of the right voltage: it should turn smoothly and quietly. Spin the turbine meter wheel by hand: it should move freely.

notes:
## What's worth keeping and why

- **Salt.** Softener salt is plain sodium chloride in pellets, blocks or crystals, usually in 10–25 kg bags. It cures hides and meat for storage, de-ices paths and makes brine. Salt for eating should say "food grade" on the bag: softener salt can carry anti-caking or rust-removing additives. Kept dry it lasts for ever.
- **Control valve head.** A moulded valve body with seals, discs or a piston, and a drain port: a ready-made multi-way water valve for a filter or timed watering. The inlet and outlet are usually 19–25 mm (3/4–1 in) threads.
- **Gear motor and board.** A small 12–24 V timer motor that turns a cam, and a board with a timer, display and buttons. The motor runs from a 12 V battery; the board needs its own transformer.
- **Turbine meter.** On metered units, a small impeller with a magnet and a Hall or reed sensor that gives a pulse for a fixed amount of water. With a counter it makes a flow meter for a tank or an irrigation line.
- **Resin tank.** A tough wound-fibreglass vessel with a plastic liner, rated for mains pressure (often 6–10 bar; read the label). Fill it with sand, gravel or granular carbon for a pressure filter, or use it as a filter column.
- **Resin.** Ion-exchange beads that swap the calcium and magnesium that make water hard for sodium. To recharge them, run a strong salt solution through the bed, then rinse it with clean water for 10–15 minutes to wash the salt out. Resin does not kill germs: soft water is not safe water.
- **Brine tank.** A 100–250 litre polyethylene tank with a lid: a rain butt, a washing tub or a store for water for animals and gardens. Treat any water from it before you drink it (boil it, filter it, or see skill_solar_disinfection).
- **Hoses and fittings.** Brine tube, drain hose and clamps.

## Variations

- Some softeners (Kinetico is the best known) run on water pressure alone, with no motor, board or plug. You get the valve and tanks only.
- Twin-tank units have two resin tanks and a bigger valve.
- Commercial and hotel units have tanks of 50 kg or more when full. Leave them unless you have lifting gear (see safety_lifting).
- Whole-house filters and well-water iron filters look similar and come apart the same way.

## What to leave

- The water left inside the tanks. It is stagnant and salty, and not for drinking.
- Resin that is black, slimy or crumbled.
